inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation (cash-flow add-back), FY2025 10-K: $73M. Corroborated by EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationTaxBenefitFromCompensationExpense of $9M. SBC fell from $1,568M (FY2022) to $220M (FY2023), $24M (FY2024) and $73M (FY2025); the tax-benefit series falls in step, so this is a real change in how UPS pays people (more incentive pay in cash, plus forfeitures reversed), not a tagging gap. No separate equity-award withholding line is tagged.
inputs.share_count_basis: 851M diluted weighted-average shares, Q2-2026 10-Q (WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding). Held FLAT. SBC is close to zero and expensed in the flows. Buybacks were $1.0B in FY2025 and nil in H1-2026, so the count is not shrinking.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD build. Risk-free rate ~4.3% (10y UST), beta ~1.0, ERP 5.0%, so cost of equity ~9.3-9.5%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0%, ~3.8% after tax. Weights ~80/20 equity/debt at market (about $79B market cap vs ~$20B net debt), giving ~8.3%. Rounded to 8.5% and held the same in every scenario: cyclical, labour and Amazon risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842. Operating-lease cost (~$954M cash in FY2025) is already an operating expense inside EBITDA, so the $4.46B of operating-lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt (treatment B for operating leases). Finance leases are small (~$133M/yr principal), sit inside total_debt and are treated as debt (treatment A). Each lease class is charged once.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI of $32M (2026-06-30) deducted in the equity bridge. The flows are consolidated. The amount is immaterial.
inputs.pension_treatment: The flows are built on EBITDA, which carries only pension SERVICE cost. Cash contributions above that (FY2025 $1,361M total contributions) fund the existing deficit. So the balance-sheet deficit (PensionAndOtherPostretirementDefinedBenefitPlansLiabilitiesNoncurrent $6,341M at 2026-06-30) goes into the equity bridge after tax at 24%, giving -$4,819M. It is charged once, as a debt-like claim, and not also inside the flows.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, with the cyclical adaptations (references/owner-fcf.md plus owner-fcf-adaptations.md: leases, pension, risk charged once). UPS is an integrated parcel and logistics operating company, not a bank, REIT, holdco or shell, and there is no prior memory entry. Fresh build: no prior DCF or Drivers file existed. FY0 is FY2025 (revenue $88,661M, GAAP EBITDA $11,613M = 13.1%, D&A $3,746M = 4.2%, capex $3,685M = 4.2%, OCF $8,450M, reported FCF $4,765M). Owner FCF = 4,765 - 73 SBC - 0 interest income = $4,692M. UPS has net DEBT of $19.8B, so there is no interest-income strip. Reported FCF is after ~$1.0B of interest paid. The engine builds unlevered flows and deducts net debt once, so interest is not double-counted. Net debt = total debt $24,484M (incl. current $634M and finance leases) - cash $4,653M at 2026-06-30. Marketable securities (~$68M at Sep-25, not tagged at Jun-26) are ignored as immaterial. MID-CYCLE, NOT PEAK: FY2021-22 EBITDA margins of 16.2% were the pandemic peak. The FY2016-2025 ten-year average GAAP EBITDA margin is ~14.2%. The base case matures at 14.5%, which is mid-cycle plus a partial, net-of-wage-inflation credit for the Network of the Future $3B savings target. It does NOT return to the peak. FY2026 margin is set at 12.5%, below the ~13.8% implied by guided adjusted operating profit of $8.65B plus D&A, because transformation and buyout cash costs (~$891M charge, up to 7,500 driver buyouts) are real cash this year. H1-2026 GAAP EBITDA was only 9.5% of revenue, partly non-cash impairments from facility closures. FY2026 revenue growth of 2.9% ties to the guided ~$91.2B and includes the Andlauer Healthcare acquisition (~$1.97B of acquisition cash in FY2025). Cap multiple: 13x base, 12x bear, 14x bull (cyclical range, never pandemic-peak multiples). Gordon at 8.5%/2% is ~15.7x, so the cap binds. Buybacks: $1.0B in FY2025, nil in H1-2026, and dividends of ~$5.4B/yr absorb essentially all FCF. The flat count is a modelling convention that the company is not currently funding with repurchases.
inputs.dividend_note: Dividends paid were $5,398M in FY2025 and $2,708M in H1-2026, against FY2025 reported FCF of $4,765M. FY2025 FCF did not cover the dividend, and FY2026 guidance of ~$5.5B FCF barely does. The DCF values the owner flows, not the dividend. A dividend paid above FCF is funded by debt and shows up in future net debt, not in this valuation.

equity_bridge.item: Pension and post-retirement deficit, after tax (6,341 x (1-0.24))

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: revenue path anchored to FY2026 guidance (+2.9%), then ~2.5-3% nominal (10-year revenue CAGR of 4.3% includes the pandemic surge; the 5-year is 0.9%)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGRs are meaningless. FY2020 equity was $669M after mark-to-market pension losses (US GAAP MTM accounting), so the 5-year equity CAGR reads 89%. EPS 5-year (33%) starts from the same depressed FY2020 base. Both diverge by more than 30% from revenue. Neither is used.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs are ABOVE reported FCF CAGRs (5-year +2.0% vs -1.1%). This is the opposite of the usual pattern: SBC fell from $1.57B in FY2022 to $73M in FY2025, so less of today's cash flow is being paid away in stock than at the peak. The 3-year declines run from the FY2022 pandemic peak and describe the cycle unwinding, not the trend.

base.narrative: The Amazon glide-down completes in 2026 and replacement SMB, healthcare and B2B volume refills the network at higher yield. Revenue tracks guidance and then grows with nominal GDP. Network of the Future savings lift EBITDA margin back to mid-cycle 14.5% by FY2029, but the 2028 Teamsters contract and wage escalators absorb roughly half of the $3B gross savings. Capex runs slightly above D&A to fund automation and cold-chain.

bull.narrative: Healthcare and cold-chain logistics (first $3B quarter, $2B investment programme) and the SMB Digital Access Program compound at high single digits, and freight-forwarding gains come from supply-chain diversification away from China. Most of the $3B automation saving reaches the bottom line, and EBITDA margin returns to ~16%, the FY2015-16 and FY2021-22 level, by FY2030. This is a full recovery, not peak-plus.

bear.narrative: Replacement volume does not arrive on schedule. The flat Q3 domestic guide turns into a FY2027 revenue decline as Amazon's own network takes more low-end parcels, and de minimis and tariff disruption keeps the US-China lanes impaired. Automation savings are consumed by the next Teamsters contract and by restructuring friction, so EBITDA margin stalls at ~12.5%, around the FY2018/FY2020 trough. The dividend is then funded with debt, or cut.

scenario_narratives.base: Amazon exit completes, SMB/healthcare refills the network, and margins recover to the 14.5% mid-cycle level (not the 16% pandemic peak) as automation savings net of wage inflation land by FY2029.
scenario_narratives.bull: Healthcare, cold-chain and SMB mix compound, and most of the $3B Network of the Future saving survives the 2028 labour contract. Margin returns to ~16% by FY2030.
scenario_narratives.bear: Volume lost to Amazon's own network and tariffs is not replaced, labour costs absorb the savings, and margin stays at ~12.5%. Dividend coverage breaks.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear is raised to 30% from the 15% default. The thesis rests on an unfinished restructuring (hub closures, 30k job cuts, Teamsters friction) carried out while demand is soft, and FCF only just covers the dividend. Base is 50%: guidance was raised after Q2-2026, so the turnaround is tracking. Bull is cut to 20% because it needs several independent things to go right at once: healthcare growth, savings retained through the 2028 contract, and stable trade policy.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Mid-cycle, transition-adjusted owner-FCF DCF. The base case does not extrapolate the FY2021-22 peak (16% EBITDA margin, $9-10B FCF) or the trough H1-2026 GAAP print. Margins recover only to the ten-year average plus a partial automation credit, and every scenario's terminal value is capped at 12-14x FCF. The pension deficit and NCI are deducted as debt-like claims after net debt.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin recovery is the whole case. Each 1pp of mature EBITDA margin is worth roughly $0.9B a year of FCF, about $13/share at a 13x exit.
The 2028 Teamsters contract could absorb the Network of the Future savings.
Volume loss to Amazon Logistics is secular, not cyclical.
Dividend above FCF in FY2025 raises leverage and could force a cut, which is a sentiment risk not captured in IV.
Pension deficit is sensitive to discount rates; it is deducted at the 2026-06-30 book value.
FY2026 guidance figures (revenue ~$91.2B, operating profit ~$8.65B, FCF ~$5.5B) are taken from the qualitative analysis and were not re-verified against the Q2-2026 8-K.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 82.00-122.41
